Hey, just a heads up. You can set yourself up to build stuff at home with a few tools. First, get a wire feeder for about $2,000.00 or less. Just look at all the models available and pick one that comes with stick welding cable and can be set up for TIG as well. You won't need the TIG settings right off but you might want to get a rig for that later. Make sure it can be used with gas shielding. Then you will rent a cylinder with CO2 Argon mix and a flow meter which should come with the welder. You're set to weld. You're machine should have two power cables, one for 120 ac and one for 240 ac. I suggest your garage have a 240 outlet installed as the power usage is more efficient and provides better welding current. However, 120 will work fine if you don't use a long extension cord and use outlets closest to the breaker panel. Less drop in voltage that way.

Then you will need an 4 and a half inch angle grinder. Always wear safety glasses and even a grinding shield. Welding gloves of course but for home usage you can get by with just some regular leather work gloves. More comfortable also than standard welding gloves. For your welding hood start with at least number twelve and I prefer the plastic gold lens. Gold film provides accurate color so you can judge the heat of your metal better. On thin metal you can see when your base metal is over heated and stop to let it cool. With green tinted lenses often you can't determine heat and the base metal will drop out and leave a hole for you to patch. Not pretty.

And that's about all you need to get started. You can practice on odd bits of scrap to get your technique down. Actually, I think no one is really a welding expert, not even me.
